taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-17, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 21.0 | 3.05 | 3.05
2 | 251.5 | 15.26 | 18.31
3 | 420.6 | 1.34 | 19.65
4 | 513.2 | 0.88 | 20.53
5 | 496.2 | 17.89 | 38.42
6 | 4573.6 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAKH-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the VES curve type, we examine each group of three consecutive layers based on their resistivities:

1. **Layers 1–2–3**: $21.0 < 251.5 < 420.6 \ (\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3) \rightarrow \mathbf{A}$
2. **Layers 2–3–4**: $251.5 < 420.6 < 513.2 \ (\rho_2 < \rho_3 < \rho_4) \rightarrow \mathbf{A}$
3. **Layers 3–4–5**: $420.6 < 513.2 > 496.2 \ (\rho_3 < \rho_4 > \rho_5) \rightarrow \mathbf{K}$
4. **Layers 4–5–6**: $513.2 > 496.2 < 4573.6 \ (\rho_4 > \rho_5 < \rho_6) \rightarrow \mathbf{H}$

Combining these gives **AAKH**, so the classification on file is correct.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "AAKH"}
